chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from Zur'ah from Samaan, who said:
I asked him about the captive whom the polytheists capture, and prayer time approaches, but the one who captured him prevents him from praying. He said: 'He gestures with a nod.'
The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: 'And the sick person prays standing while having the ability, up to his saying, and it is disliked.'

key_terms.إِيمَاءً: Gesturing (a specific type of abbreviated prayer)
key_terms.الْأَسِير: The captive or prisoner of war
key_terms.الْمُشْرِكُونَ: The polytheists (often referring to the enemy in this context)

ai.seo_question: How should a prisoner perform prayer if they are prevented from doing the full ritual by their captors?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *darura* (necessity) in worship, ruling that a captive prevented from standing or reciting by his captors may pray by gesturing (*i'nam*), mirroring the concession for the sick. Sheikh al-Tusi’s note highlights the continuity of this ruling, linking the captive’s situation to that of a patient who prays standing despite having the ability, thereby emphasizing the flexibility of *salat* under duress. This reflects the Shia juristic view that the essence of prayer remains valid even when physical conditions are compromised by external force or illness.
